answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to earn standing through a slow, verifiable work history, like a reef that grows only over time. A newcomer enters through a narrow inlet: it must complete useful, checkable tasks under one persistent identity before it can transact or vote. Copying one identity into many is useless, because each copy starts empty and must pay the same time and computation cost again. Even a sonnet of fake credentials cannot shortcut that history, so creating thousands of Sybils becomes far more expensive than the reward they could steal.
